samples.summary: Seed script re-implements the public-tier enforcement gate instead of calling assertYorkieAuthEnforced
samples.evidence: The previous code reused `isYorkieAuthEnforced`; the delta replaces that with an inline `config.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') !== 'true'` while the comment itself says "the same explicit affirmation the server demands at submit/approve — see assertYorkieAuthEnforced". `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/template/template-review.ts:91) is exported from a module this file already imports (`parseReviewerIds`), so the reuse was available and free. Two copies of one policy will drift the moment the gate's reading changes again (it just changed in this very delta), and the seed script would then accept or refuse runs the server does not.

samples.summary: Yorkie token minting duplicated outside AuthService, including the secret/expiry convention
samples.evidence: AuthService is the single place that mints Yorkie webhook tokens (`issueYorkieUserToken`, `issueYorkieShareToken`, auth.service.ts:74-87), owning `accessSecret` and `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN ?? '10m'` (auth.service.ts:68-70). The new module constructs its own bare `JwtService`, and `YorkieService` (yorkie.service.ts:44-56) re-reads `JWT_SECRET` and re-hardcodes the same `'10m'` default. The DI-free rationale is stated, but a third mint site means the secret choice and expiry default now live in two places and can diverge silently (e.g. a future JWT_YORKIE_SECRET split would break server-side attaches only).

samples.summary: template-gallery.md still explains the enforcement gate by the old shadow-by-default rationale the delta replaced
samples.evidence: The delta rewrites `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` to demand a literal `true` *because* an unset variable says nothing about whether the auth-webhook methods were registered (template-review.ts:60-95), and the webhook's own default is now enforce. But the canonical design doc still says "with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only *shadows*" as the reason the tier refuses to operate. A reader of the design doc gets a rationale that no longer matches either the code or docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:29 ("Enforcement itself is the default").

samples.summary: sharing.md still documents shadow mode as the default for YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE
samples.evidence: "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode" contradicts the enforce-by-default reading this PR ships (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:29, yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts). The delta is what makes enforce-by-default actually workable server-side, so the doc set it depends on should be consistent; may have been raised in an earlier round.

samples.summary: Standalone backend Yorkie maintenance scripts still attach with no auth token, which enforce-by-default now breaks
samples.evidence: The delta's premise is that every server-side attach must identify itself or 401 wherever the webhook methods are registered. All of packages/backend/src goes through `YorkieService`, but `scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:204-210`, `scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:340` and `scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:214` construct raw `yorkie.Client`s with no `authTokenInjector`, so those operator tools fail on exactly the deployments this change targets. Either they should mint a service token too, or the design doc's new paragraph should scope them out.
